{{Quote|Is it compulsory to like ''gihaal?"<br />"''I doubt it. I think a lot of Mandos hate it, too.|[[Ruusaan Skirata]] and [[Nyreen Vollen]]|<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>}}
'''''Gihaal''''' was a dried [[Fish/Legends|fishmeal]] mixture, its name drawn simply from the word for "fishmeal" in the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']].<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> Prepared from raw, freshly gutted fish, the meat was [[Fire/Legends|smoked]] and dried before being packaged into sealed containers for preservation.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Richly nourishing, ''gihaal'' provided a combination of fat and [[Protein/Legends|protein]], and could remain edible for [[Standard year/Legends|years]] without the need for [[Conservator|refrigeration]].<ref name="TMPaC" /> Because of these traits, ''gihaal'' became a staple in Mandalorian field [[Food rations|rations]], though its pungently unpleasant odor was off-putting to many Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]].<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

The Mandalorian [[Jun Hokan]] enjoyed ''gihaal'', and during a mission to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mes Cavoli]] in [[72 BBY/Legends|72 BBY]], Hokan ate ''gihaal'' shavings he carved from a larger chunk with a [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblade]], in the same manner in which many other individuals ate [[Fruit/Legends|fruit]].<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref> After [[Gender/Legends|his]] dealings with the [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoan]] [[Cloning/Legends|cloners]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]], the ''[[Cuy'val Dar]]'' [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commando]] training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]] [[Kal Skirata]] took to pejoratively referring to the ancestrally [[Water/Legends|aquatic]] Kaminoans as ''gihaal''. This habit spread among a number of other Mandalorian ''Cuy'val Dar'' sergeants, as well as their [[Commando/Legends|commando]] trainees.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

Following the [[Declaration of a New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], and in celebration of the arrival of [[Spring/Legends|spring]] in the north of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]<ref name="ImpCom501st" />—the cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Mandalorian people, located in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>—the members of [[Clan Skirata]] prepared a large meal that included portions of preserved ''gihaal''.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''Gihaal'' is a dried fishmeal mixture, like pemmican...|[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]|<ref name="TMPaC" />}}
''Gihaal'' first entered ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] with a mention in the [[2006]] novel, ''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]'' by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]].<ref name="TZ">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref> It was further featured as an insult in Traviss' short-story ''[[Odds]]'',<ref name="Odds">{{InsiderCite|87|Odds}}</ref> and the sequel to ''Triple Zero'' in the [[Republic Commando|''Republic'' and ''Imperial Commando'' series]], [[Republic Commando: True Colors|''True Colors'']].<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> With the release of the series' fourth novel, [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], ''gihaal'' finally made its first true appearance,<ref name="O66" /> before appearing again in the following novel, ''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

In the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article, ''[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]'', published in [[February]] of [[2006]] as part of the magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth issue]], ''gihaal'' was discussed in relation to its place in traditional Mandalorian cuisine. The dish's creator, Karen Traviss, likens ''gihaal'' to real-world [[:Wikipedia:Pemmican|pemmican]], a food traditionally created by a number of [[:Wikipedia:Native Americans|Native American]] peoples.<ref name="TMPaC" />
